author: Aristophanes
evidence: Italian ex-libris 'De miser Marco Musuro' (Musurus, in Italy c. 1486-1517) and 'Questo libro e de mi Andronico Manolesso'; Latin note of Francesco Barbaro, Venetian patrician
sources: Review of N. G. Wilson, Aristophanis Fabulae (OCT 2007), Emerita (sigla R, V, A, K, E, M, U) https://emerita.revistas.csic.es/index.php/emerita/article/download/320/329/321

author: Aeschylus; Sophocles
role: Aeschylus F, a main witness for the Agamemnon and Eumenides; also Sophocles Za
evidence: In the Medici library (the Laurentian, opened 1571)
sources: ParaText (Pavia): Laur. plut. 31.8 https://paratext.unipv.it/?p=1264 | Aeschylus' ManTra project (Sapienza): 'the so-called Aeschylus Farnese Neap. II F 31' https://research.uniroma1.it/node/103633

author: Aeschylus; Sophocles
role: Aeschylus G, one of the three key witnesses (with F and T) for the Agamemnon and Eumenides
evidence: In the Marciana's appendix of later legacies; no pre-1600 evidence in Zanetti.
sources: Aeschylus' ManTra project (Sapienza): 'the so-called Aeschylus Farnese Neap. II F 31' https://research.uniroma1.it/node/103633

author: Hesiod; Homer
role: Hesiod B, the oldest medieval witness of the Theogony and Shield; also Iliad Y in West
evidence: In the Supplément grec (acquired after 1740); no pre-1600 evidence found.
sources: R. Pearse, Some manuscript traditions of the Greek classics (sigla after West, Most, etc.) https://www.tertullian.org/rpearse/manuscripts/greek_classics.htm

author: [Longinus]; Aristotle (pseudo-)
role: Archetype of On the Sublime (P): all other copies descend from it
evidence: Catherine de' Medici's inventory of 1589 (entry identified)

author: Plutarch
role: Principal witness of the Lives (U in Ziegler), parchment
status: In the Vatican before 1600; its entry of 1475 not identified
evidence: Old Vatican pluteus mark of about the mid-16th c. (Mercati); counted with the 1475 inventory's unidentified entries.
sources: E. Muntz and P. Fabre, La Bibliotheque du Vatican au XVe siecle (1887), catalog record https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/000818337.marc

author: Theophrastus
work: History of Plants; Causes of Plants
role: Principal witness (U) of both botanical works
evidence: Federico's arms as duke (FE. DVX / F. D.); old Urbino inventory (Indice vecchio, Urb. lat. 1671) Greek no. 48

author: Plotinus
role: Plotinus A (Henry-Schwyzer), head of one family
evidence: In the Medici library (the Laurentian, opened 1571)

author: Cassius Dio
role: Dio L, principal witness for books 36-60 with M (Marc. gr. 395)
evidence: In the Medici library (the Laurentian, opened 1571)

author: Xenophon
role: Anabasis C, the best manuscript of the Anabasis, dated 1320
evidence: Catherine de' Medici's inventory of 1589 (entry identified)

author: Xenophon
role: Principal witness for Xenophon's minor works (A in Marchant's OCT)
evidence: Fulvio Orsini's library (his inventory of 1600).

author: Diodorus Siculus
role: Diodorus C, one of the two oldest witnesses for books I-V (with D, Naples suppl. gr. 4)
evidence: Arrived in the Vatican Library in 1553 (P. Bertrac and Y. Vernière, Diodorus, Budé ed., vol. 1); a parchment codex, so not one of the paper Diodorus entries of 1455 and 1475
sources: R. Pearse, 'Diodorus Siculus: the manuscripts' (after Bertrac-Verniere, Bude ed. I, 1993) https://www.tertullian.org/rpearse/manuscripts/diodorus_sicilus.htm

author: Archimedes
work: Works (Sphere and Cylinder, Measurement of the Circle, Conoids, Spirals, Plane Equilibria, Sand-reckoner, Quadrature of the Parabola, etc.)
role: Heiberg's A, archetype of all surviving Greek Archimedes manuscripts except the palimpsest C
evidence: Used by William of Moerbeke at the papal court (Viterbo, 1269); the papal inventory of 1311, no. 612; later Giorgio Valla's; lost after 1564.
sources: A. Jones, William of Moerbeke, the Papal Greek Manuscripts, and the Collection of Pappus in Vat. gr. 218, Scriptorium 40 (1986) https://philarchive.org/archive/CLAAIT-14 | historyofinformation.com, survival of Archimedes' works (codices A, B, C) https://historyofinformation.com/detail.php?id=2864

author: Archimedes
work: Plane Equilibria, Quadrature of the Parabola, Floating Bodies
role: Heiberg's B; only source (through Moerbeke's Latin) of On Floating Bodies until the palimpsest was found
evidence: Used by William of Moerbeke with codex A (Viterbo, 1269); said to be in the papal inventories of 1295 and 1311; lost. Added in 0.10.
sources: historyofinformation.com, survival of Archimedes' works (codices A, B, C) https://historyofinformation.com/detail.php?id=2864 | A. Jones, review of Netz et al., The Archimedes Palimpsest (2005) https://archive.nyu.edu/bitstream/2451/60924/2/Jones%202005%20rev%20Netz%20Archimedes.pdf

author: Archimedes
work: Method, Stomachion, Floating Bodies (Greek), and other works
role: Heiberg's C; unique Greek witness of the Method, Stomachion and Floating Bodies
evidence: In Jerusalem and Constantinople, where Heiberg identified it in 1906; one leaf taken by Tischendorf in the 1840s.
sources: historyofinformation.com, survival of Archimedes' works (codices A, B, C) https://historyofinformation.com/detail.php?id=2864 | A. Jones, review of Netz et al., The Archimedes Palimpsest (2005) https://archive.nyu.edu/bitstream/2451/60924/2/Jones%202005%20rev%20Netz%20Archimedes.pdf

author: Hippocrates
work: Works (Internal Affections, Diseases of Women, etc.)
role: Hippocrates theta (Littré's theta), one of the oldest independent witnesses
evidence: Busbecq's purchase note: "ab Augerio Busbeckio ... olim fuit comparatus Constantinopoli"
sources: J. Irigoin, Collège de France course summary 1987-1988 (Hippocratic tradition) https://www.college-de-france.fr/sites/default/files/media/document/2023-03/1987-1988_irigoin.pdf | E. Serafinová, Beobachtungen zum Codex Vindobonensis Medicus graecus 4 (2011) https://real.mtak.hu/43774/

author: Aristarchus, Autolycus, Euclid, Theodosius, Hypsicles
work: 'Little Astronomy' collection (Sizes and Distances; Moving Sphere; Phaenomena; Optics; Spherics)
role: oldest and principal witness of the 'Little Astronomy' (e.g. Aristarchus, Autolycus)
status: In the Vatican before 1600; its entry of 1475 not identified
evidence: Supplemented in the Vatican by Ioannes Honorios (c. 1535-1563); perhaps the 1475 entry 'Theodosii Sperica, et Euclidis Phenomena. Ex membr.'; counted with the 1475 inventory's unidentified entries.
sources: Vatican exhibit, Greek mathematics (Vat. gr. 204) https://ibiblio.org/expo/vatican.exhibit/exhibit/d-mathematics/Greek_math2.html

author: Old Testament
role: Rahlfs 108, a leading Lucianic witness and the main exemplar of the Complutensian Polyglot
status: In the Vatican before 1600; its entry of 1475 not identified
evidence: In the Vatican before Leo X lent it for the Complutensian Polyglot (c. 1512-1517; returned 1518); counted with the 1475 inventory's unidentified entries.

author: Old Testament
role: Codex Coislinianus, Rahlfs M, principal uncial for the Octateuch with hexaplaric notes
evidence: Bought in the East for Chancellor Pierre Séguier (17th c.).
sources: H. B. Swete, Introduction to the Old Testament in Greek, ch. V https://biblehub.Com/library/swete/an_introduction_to_the_old_testament_in_greek_additional_notes/chapter_v_manuscripts_of_the.htm

author: Galen
work: On the Avoidance of Grief (De indolentia) and other works
role: unique witness of De indolentia; fuller Greek of On My Own Opinions
evidence: Still at the Vlatadon monastery in Thessalonica.
